thread:
arjun: Heads up — p95 tail for decode + attention jumped ~18% on main after last night's merge. Seeing lots of fallbacks to attn_quant_fallback for fp8-backed models. attaching quick perf snap:

arjun: ```profile summary
model: redwood-7b-quant-fp8
seq_len=512, requests=1200
fast_attn_calls: 58
fallback_attn_calls: 420
avg_token_latency_ms: 92 -> was 78 last week
kv_evictions_per_min: 3.2 -> was 0.4
```

sarah: yikes. fallback count is huge. any hints from the selector logs?

arjun: selector logs show a new safety path triggered when transpose alignment != 64 bytes after commit 8f1b2c4. the selector chooses the slower fallback kernel that does an unoptimized matmul.

devon: starting a bisect now, will chew through merges from yesterday. focusing on PRs that touched quant packer / transpose ordering.

lina: noticed a KV eviction spike correlated with the same window; could be longer per-token time causing cache churn. attaching a small kv timeline snippet:

lina: ```kv timeline
00:00:00 request A seq512 -> cache miss
00:00:00.09 request B seq256 -> cache evict key X
00:00:00.18 request C seq512 -> miss again
```

perf-bot: CI perf job perf/e2e-decode-512 reported p95 +12% vs baseline (threshold exceeded)

deploy-bot: Canary rolled back to v1.23.4 due to latency alert :warning:

arjun: I'm going to try a narrow revert of the transpose reordering in 8f1b2c4 as a hotfix. also adding an intermediate tmp flag to skip the safety check for our known fp8 models to validate impact. can someone run local perf with `--seq-len 512 --concurrency 8`?

devon: on it. also adding a quick assertion in the selector logs to dump alignment details and kernel decision (`selector.debug=true`). will run bisect in parallel.

sarah: if the safety check is overly conservative we can tighten it to check exact model quant params rather than generic alignment. but we should QA for correctness first.

arjun: agreed. temp hotfix: set `attn_kernel_priority=[matmul_fast, attn_quant_fallback]` for seq<256 in our canary deployment to reduce P99 impact; will only flip if regression confirmed.

lina: :thumbsup: scheduling a small canary rollout after devon posts perf numbers.

devon: bisect narrows to 8f1b2c4 -> the transpose reorder combined with a micro-optimization in the quant packer changes the alignment by 16 bytes on some tensors. reverting that line brings fallback_attn_calls down to 12 in my local run. preparing revert PR #4678.

arjun: nice. please include the small regression test that asserts fallback_attn_calls < 50 for seq=512 in CI. I'll open a rollback ticket and ping SLOs/ops.

sarah: after revert + targeted CI guard we should follow up with a proper fix: either adjust the kernel selector to be model-aware or make the fallback kernel faster (vectorize the matmul).

devon: PR #4678 opened, perf numbers attached in the PR checks. canary redeploy queued.

arjun: thanks all — monitoring traces now and will post updates. if anyone sees KV churn still high after the revert shout here.

lina: noted. will keep an eye on cache hit-rate dashboards.

perf-bot: Watcher: alert cleared on canary after redeploy to reverted variant (p95 back within 3% of baseline).

arjun: great, closing the immediate rollback. follow-up: add a small perf test to detect alignment-induced fallbacks and a selector unit test to avoid regression next time.

sarah: sounds good. I'll create a short ticket for selector improvements and QA checklist.

devon: adding CI perf guard: `assert(fallback_attn_calls / total_attn_calls < 0.05)` in nightly perf job.

arjun: perfect. thanks everyone.
